title: The Ribbon S is the logo: app icon, browser tab and header
body: The owner picked option 12 from the logo board: an S drawn as one thick ribbon in seven color segments. It replaces the page-with-lines icon on the home screen and in the browser tab, and now sits beside the name at the top of the app, where it follows the colors chosen in Editor.

title: Make the chat add-on installable in one step
body:
The add-on that colors Claude's replies was only ever attached to the session that wrote it, so no other chat loaded it. The repository now lists it as a plugin, which Claude Code can install for every session:

claude plugin install synesthetic-chat --marketplace mrwells1216/Synethetics-Layer

title: Owner's notes: marks first, DEV under the green bar, a tool bar, an honest Formula
body:
From five notes left in the app:

- Screenshots and highlights now show only the marks first (Good, Not good, Fix/idea). Picking one opens the comment window, with Submit and Skip. A comment is optional for every mark. - Text in the example document can be highlighted and triple-clicked. It lives in a frame of its own, which the tools never listened to. - The Formula shows each kind the way it lands in real text: only the matched words carry the look, and each look is named beside its kind. The link example used a web address the app would not have matched. The grammar layer's four shapes are listed too. - Adverbs are thin italic. The fonts that have a thin face now load it. - The example's controls are one compact tool bar of joined buttons. - DEV is a pill under the green bar, and the green slot of the phone strip. The bar lights up while the tools are on.

title: Fix the hosted app failing to start: pin the lighter PDF library
body: pymupdf 2.1 pulls in onnxruntime, networkx and two layout packages that the app never uses. Installing them when the hosted function starts filled its temporary disk, and every page returned a server error. pymupdf 1.28.2 has no extra dependencies and passes the same tests.

title: One DEV switch at the top; grammar words differ by shape, not only color
body:
Change developer mode to a single switch in the header. On, you can highlight text to mark it and triple-click for a screenshot; off, none of it runs. Notes need no setup: where the site has no store they are kept on the device, with Copy for Claude and Share with pictures in Settings.

Remove the DEV button, its Live, Fixes and State panel, the request and error recorder, and the linking controls in Settings.

Add shape to the grammar layer on pages and in kept-layout PDF, Word and Excel files: verbs bold, adjectives italic, adverbs italic with a dotted underline, nouns a plain tint.

The screenshot frame gets a soft spectrum border and tinted corners.

title: Highlight notes get Good and Not good; the side strip steps aside for results
body:
Highlighting text in developer mode now offers Good, Not good and Fix/idea, like the screenshot window. Good and Not good can be saved without a note.

Fix the phone tab strip covering the Open button in the result view: the strip slides away while a result or the roller is open.

Fix screenshots picking up a "Saved" toast, and the live panel adding a new listener each time it opened.

The chat style sheet now names the right place in Claude's settings, uses a sans font for colored words and lists light mode colors.

title: Add a chat style sheet: Claude replies in the app's colors and looks
body: docs/chat-style-instructions.md is ready to paste into Claude's preferences. It has plain markdown cues that work everywhere, real color through inline math using the app's default colors, and an HTML page for long answers.

title: Make the plus part of the name: Synesthetic+
body: The + is now a letter of the name: the same font, size and weight, set right against the "c", in the next color of the name's color cycle. It is filled while the phone tab strip is out and an outline while it's away.

title: ALL CAPS headers with a color line behind, Formula and Customize
body: Headers across the app are in ALL CAPS with a line in their page's tab color running behind the letters. "What gets a color" is now Formula and "See it on real writing" is Customize. The live roller previews show each color's underline too. On phones the color bars scroll away while the side strip is out, and stay pinned at the top only when it's hidden.

title: Add bold, italic and underline to each color's look
body: Every category now has bold, italic, an underline style (solid, dotted, dashed, double, wavy or none) and an underline color that can differ from its text color, set in Editor beside ALL CAPS and size. Each example shows its look. Underlines are thicker and show in every highlight style, and the look carries into Free Rain, the examples, converted pages, and PDF, Word and Excel files (Excel underlines are single or double, in the text's color).

title: Thinner plus, and one smooth motion for the tab strip
body: The plus after the name is thinner and has no glow. The phone tab strip slides the same way out and back (sideways, no squish or fade), and all seven header bars light up together in one pulse each time. Opening the page no longer plays the slide.

title: Side strip floats over the page; a glowing plus shows or hides it
body: On phones the seven-color tab strip is now the top layer over the page instead of pushing it over. The spectrum button is gone: a plus after the name (Synesthetic+) with a slow colorful glow shows or hides the strip, filled while it's out and an outline while it's away.

title: Add a side strip of the seven colors for tabs on phones
body: On phones the tab names move to a strip down the right edge, one color per tab and the green center left blank, each name on one line reading bottom to top. The open tab sticks out. The seven bars stay at the top. A small spectrum button folds the strip up into the header (the bars ripple as it lands) and opens it again from there.

title: Tighter color bars, and tab names in their bar's color by default
body: The bars sit closer together, and each tab name now takes its bar's color unless Settings, Tab names says otherwise.

title: Find the fix storage however Vercel named it
body: Connecting a Blob store can give its variables a custom prefix; the server now finds the store's token and id by their values. The dev key is trimmed, so a pasted space or line break doesn't lock developer mode.

title: Bring back the 7th color bar, and add tab name styles to try
body: The center (green) bar is a color only, not a tab; Editor, Saved and Settings move to the last three bars. Settings, Tab names switches between Plain, In their color (each name in its bar's color) and Highlighted (each name highlighted in its bar's color, letters in the page color, line by line like the core chips). Screenshots in developer mode keep the style.

title: Change log tags read only what a change says it did
body: A description that merely mentions "fixed" or "removed" no longer adds those tags; only a sentence that starts with Fix or Remove does.

title: Add developer mode and a change log in Settings
body:
Developer mode is a layer for fixing the app: highlight text and press Fix/idea, or triple-click (triple-tap) for a screenshot frame to move, resize and mark Good, Not good or Fix/idea. The DEV button shows live requests, errors, warnings and state. Notes are append-only and wait for the next Claude session (python fixes.py list), which closes each with what it did. Hosted, they go to a private Vercel Blob store and only devices opened with the dev link can save or read them.

What's new lists every change to main, tagged Added, Changed, Fixed or Removed, with a filter.

title: PDF words get their new look, and a long market wrap sample
body: PDFs: matched words are redrawn in place with your colors, fonts, ALL CAPS and sizes (the old word is covered with the paper color around it, so nothing moves); highlight notes stay as an option. Word and Excel pick up the category fonts and bold. A 3-page made-up S&P 500 weekly wrap to try in Synesthesize and How it works. Fixes: dates no longer run across a sentence end (September. 77), ligatures in PDFs, upload-limit replies, stale examples.

title: Six tabs under the color bars, Word Bank, rollers, Free Rain and Saved
body: How it works with famous writing and live switches; Synesthesize with a roller that colors only the parts you pick, recent thumbnails and a how-to strip; Free Rain editor with auto color, roller and rain; Editor with color schemes, ALL CAPS and size per category, and the Word Bank; Saved with list and thumbnail views, delete and undo; Settings.

title: Serve the icons and manifest behind Vercel's rewrite
Desktop layout, app icons and installable app
body: Two columns on wide screens, drop or paste a file anywhere, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter and Esc. Icons, a web manifest and an Install button so it can live on a phone home screen or a desktop.

title: Keep the original look: add the colors on top of PDF, Word and Excel files
body: PDFs get highlight (or underline) notes over matched words; Word runs are recolored in place by highlight style; Excel colors number/date cells and matched words in text cells. Switch in the web app, --keep on the CLI.

title: Color the app's own text, with a switch to turn it off
body: The page now runs the lens's content patterns over its own instructions, labels, example cards and messages, in the chosen highlight style. A switch on the home page and in Customize turns it on or off (on by default, saved per device). The copy names real examples (1,250, Aug 14, page 5, do not) so the colors show.

title: Add "Try an example" documents to the web app
body: Seven made-up documents for different uses (study notes, a lease, care instructions, a work email, a recipe, a budget table, a trip itinerary). Tapping one converts it with the reader's own colors and fonts. Each card shows the colors that document uses; the study notes turn the grammar layer on.

title: Redesign the web app and add a Customize screen for colors and fonts
body: The app is themed by the reader's own category colors: a lettered wordmark, a spectrum strip, a colored paper preview and a gradient Convert button. Customize sets each category's dark and light color, body and heading fonts, text size, highlight style and theme, with a live preview, reset, export and import. The settings are sent with each conversion (validated server side) and baked into the page; the CLI reads the exported file with --style.

title: Add web UI and Vercel deployment
body: New upload page (file or pasted text, result shown in place with Save and Open), shared by `synesthetic serve` and a Vercel Python function. File names travel in a header so they stay out of URLs and logs; size limit is per host (4.4 MB on Vercel).

title: Fix review findings: encodings, AI-layer errors, table flag, upload origin check
body: - read_text no longer decodes BOM-less cp1252 text as utf-16 garbage - claude timeouts and spawn errors become AIUnavailable; finished batches are cached when another fails; one temp folder per run, removed afterwards - PDF table detection is a parameter of extract() instead of a module global (was racy under the threaded upload server) - /convert refuses cross-site posts (Sec-Fetch-Site / Origin) and reads the body before any error so browsers see the message - plain-text: a lead-in line after a blank line no longer glues onto the previous bullet; a lone bullet line is never a heading - LibreOffice failures surface as UnsupportedFile; its temp folder is removed - template filled in one pass so {{BODY}} in document text survives - render reuses colorcheck's contrast math; chat mod reads group offsets from m.indices; small dead-code cleanups - 6 new tests (64 pass); TS parity unchanged

title: Add Synesthetic Layer: file-to-HTML color layer and Claude chat mod
body: Converts .txt, .md, .docx, .doc, .pdf and .xlsx into self-contained HTML with content-type, grammar and AI-meaning layers; includes the Claude Code chat mod, tests and the research report behind the design.
